body:
I still get "Node does not exist" error on 8.2.0-next.2 
```
Node does not exist: /Users/wuboy/workspace/xinos2-ng/node_modules/ngx-papaparse
```

If I rollback to angular/compiler-cli 8.0.3. I will show only warning:
```
WARNING in Entry point 'ngx-papaparse' contains deep imports into 'papaparse/papaparse.min.js'. This is probably not a problem, but may cause the compilation of entry points to be out of order.
```

However there are other errors in version 8.0.3. So I can't use this version.
Is there anything I can do? Should this be fixed by ngx-papaparse ?

@wuboy0307 - in this case the problem is that `ngx-papaparse` is indeed doing a deep import   `import * as lib from 'papaparse/papaparse.min.js';` rather than simply `import * as lib from 'papaparse';`.

In the latest version of ngcc the dependency checking phase is not handling this correctly. I think we should probably be more resilient to this approach.

I have got the same issue with ngx-highlightjs: 

> ERROR in Node does not exist: /Users/localadmin/D/restructure/webclients/node_modules/ngx-highlightjs

(8.2.0-rc.0)

This crash should be fixed by https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/31872 but note that this failure is probably due to a missing dependency. Try running `./node_modules/.bin/ivy-ngcc -l debug`. It should tell you if this package has a dependency that has not been installed.

> Invalid entry-point /Users/localadmin/D/restructure/webclients/node_modules/ngx-highlightjs. It is missing required dependencies:
>  - highlight.js/lib/highlight.js

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10297808/62139755-2c7d2080-b2ea-11e9-8013-668a76e5a1b5.png)


Should I open a ticket at ngx-highlightjs?

@qaxqaxqax - not just yet. Can you confirm that `highlight.js` is indeed installed in your local project? I can see from here https://unpkg.com/browse/ngx-highlightjs@3.0.3/package.json that it is only a peer dependency, in which case you must install it yourself.

Assuming that you have done this, then the problem is that ngx-hightlightjs is doing a "deep import" directly to a file in `highlight.js` rather than just a regular entry-point dependency. If so then this is a scenario that is common enough that we might want to look into fixing ngcc to cope with it...

*Edit:*
I tried it locally and it is indeed a problem with the deep import. This has occurred before with other packages so we should look at how to fix this in ngcc.... cc @JoostK :-)
